description: Every partner deal registration, approved or not. Exists as its own registry rather than a field on the opportunity because a registration is a CLAIM on an end customer that starts a protection clock — it precedes the opportunity, may never become one, and must be checkable against other partners' claims before it's approved.

columns.name: partner_id
columns.note: The partner who SUBMITTED the registration. Which tier they occupy is in distributor_id / reseller_id — a submission is not itself a claim on a tier.

columns.name: partner_rep_email
columns.note: The email domain is often the most reliable way to match a submission back to a partner

columns.name: distributor_id
columns.note: PARTNER- id of the distributor tier, if the deal has one. Blank for single-tier deals.

columns.name: reseller_id
columns.note: PARTNER- id of the reselling tier. May be the SAME partner as the distributor — a partner fulfilling both tiers is a legitimate single-partner deal, not a duplicate.

columns.name: deal_structure
columns.note: DERIVED. Two-tier = different partners at each tier. Single-tier = one partner at both, or only one tier populated. This is what tells the conflict check whether a second partner on the deal is teaming or collision.

columns.name: teaming_confirmed
columns.note: Whether both partners know they're working this together. Two partners on one deal who each think they're alone is the same problem as channel conflict, arriving later.

columns.name: end_customer_domain
columns.note: Normalised domain. Matches far more reliably than company name — 'Acme Corp', 'ACME Corporation' and 'Acme, Inc.' are one customer.

columns.name: protection_days
columns.note: From the partner agreement at time of approval, not looked up later — terms change

columns.name: protection_expires
columns.note: DERIVED: approved_date plus protection_days. After this the claim lapses and the customer is open again.

columns.name: conflict_checked
columns.note: Whether a conflict check has been run. Approving without one is how channel disputes start.

columns.name: conflict_type
columns.note: DERIVED by the conflict checker. Conflict is by TIER, not by partner.

columns.name: conflicts_with
columns.note: DEALREG- or OPP- id of whatever it collides with

columns.name: decline_reason
values: Tier already claimed by another partner
Partner not permitted in that role

columns.name: resolution_note
columns.note: How a conflict was settled. The record that stops it being re-litigated.

columns.name: owner
columns.note: Who at our end reviewed it

columns.name: crm_last_modified
columns.note: The CRM's own last-modified stamp as at the last sync. Drift detection compares it against the CRM's current value; without it, which side changed a field is a guess.

columns.name: last_synced
columns.note: When this row was last reconciled against the CRM. A last_updated later than this means the row is ahead of the CRM and owes a push.
